title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Property Preservation of Registered Trademark Rights by People's Courts

articles.content_en: When a People's Court takes property preservation measures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, if it needs to preserve a registered trademark right, it shall issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office), specifying the name of the registered trademark to be preserved with the assistance of the Trademark Office, the registrant, the registration certificate number, the preservation period, and the content of assistance in enforcement and preservation, including prohibiting transfer, cancellation of the registered trademark, modification of registration matters, and handling of trademark right pledge registration, among other matters.

The period for preserving a registered trademark right shall not exceed six months at a time, commencing from the date on which the Trademark Office receives the notice of assistance in enforcement. If it is still necessary to continue taking preservation measures for the registered trademark right, the People's Court shall re-issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the Trademark Office before the expiration of the preservation period, requesting continued preservation. Otherwise, it shall be deemed that the property preservation of the registered trademark right is automatically released.
A People's Court shall not repeatedly preserve a registered trademark right that has already been preserved.
